correctness.rationale: For any deleted set \(S\) of size \(k\), cubic edge counting gives \(2k=10+e(S)+c\) whenever the complement is a forest with \(c\) components. Thus no smaller solution exists and six-vertex optima have either \(e(S)=0,c=2\) or \(e(S)=1,c=1\). Explicit deletion masks 126 and 1244 attain those classes. The complete 38,760-subset incidence enumeration and independent generalized-Petersen union-find algorithm agree on 760 and 2,100 optima. A separate C++ search covers all 60,460 deletion sets of size at most six. All 240 explicit symmetry maps are checked and yield 19 disjoint orbits with total 2,860. The group is proved full using the five four-cliques of the triangular graph on two-subsets.

originality.rationale: Claim assessed: exact 2,860 optimum sets, 760/2,100 structure split, component-size spectrum and 19 automorphism orbits, NOT the scalar value 6. Wei--Li (2013) and Gao--Xu--Wang--Zhu--Yang (2015) studied generalized-Petersen decycling numbers and are credited for the minimum. Yang--Ren (2019) obtained a general regular-graph decycling identity encompassing the present edge-count formula. Accessible full texts of Kelly--Liu (2016), Hertz (2021), Ghalavand--Li (2025) do not present this exact enumeration. Relevant 2013 and 2015 papers were accessible at indexed abstract/metadata level only, with full text not obtained; their possible hidden enumeration remains an explicit material priority risk, and originality is not independently confirmed.

value.rationale: The result completely classifies every largest induced forest in the classical distance-transitive cubic graph of girth six, the Desargues graph, a natural extremal setting for cubic induced-forest bounds. The two distinct complement topologies (two trees versus one tree), exact component-order census and 19 symmetry classes are mathematically motivated and not determined by the minimum size. The precise coefficient and orbit representatives make the extremal structure reusable as a benchmark; no general-family contribution is assumed.
